column11: ELEVIDYS (delandistrogene moxeparvovec) wholesale acquisition cost $3.2mm per treatment: BioPharma Dive, 'Sarepta prices Duchenne gene therapy at $3.2M' (biopharmadive.com/news/sarepta-duchenne-elevidys-price-million-gene-therapy/653720/); Managed Healthcare Executive, 'First Gene Therapy for Duchenne Priced at $3.2 Million' (managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/first-gene-therapy-for-duchenne-priced-at-3-2-million). Read from search summaries; pages not opened. Book: drug_demand holds no CMS rows for ELEVIDYS (lookup.py demand Elevidys returns nothing)
column12: JUDGEMENT: parity with ELEVIDYS. Sarepta has set no price for SRP-9003. ELEVIDYS is Sarepta's only marketed gene therapy and uses the same AAVrh74 vector, the same manufacturing network (Catalent, Aldevron per the 10-Q) and the same neuromuscular infusion centres, so it is the house precedent. A published WAC beats the CMS convention, and there is no CMS row anyway. Case for higher: LGMD2E/R4 is roughly 40 times rarer than DMD (292 against 11,952 US patients), and ultra-rare one-time gene therapies list higher (e.g. Lenmeldy and Kebilidi, not sourced here); adults need more vector at a weight-based dose. Case for lower: an accelerated approval on beta-sarcoglycan expression rather than function, the AAVrh74 liver-safety record (ELEVIDYS boxed warning and non-ambulatory indication removed; a fatal case in the SRP-9004 LGMD trial), and payer resistance after ELEVIDYS

column11: Sarepta 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-335003, filed 2026-08-05, MD&A): 'In December 2025, the FDA confirmed that we remain on clinical hold and informed us that it requires data from the study of sirolimus as an immunosuppressant before accepting a biologic license application ("BLA") for SRP-9003. We anticipate re-engaging with the agency on next steps for the program after we receive data from Cohort 8 of Study 9001-103 (ENDEAVOR).' Sarepta Q2 2026 results 8-K (0001193125-26-335056, EX-99.1): full enrollment of ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 by end of 2026 and 12-week data from the full cohort in Q1 2027. EMERGENE (NCT06246513) primary completion 2025-03-04, actual (book trials table); Sarepta announced safety and expression results in October 2025 (10-Q)
column12: JUDGEMENT. Launch is gated by the clinical hold and the FDA's sirolimus requirement, not by the trial, which has read out. Earliest path: Cohort 8 data Q1 2027, re-engagement Q2 2027, BLA and hold lift in 2H 2027, an 8-month priority review, approval in 2028; 2029 is the first full year. No BLA date is filed: the 10-K says the hold 'has impacted the timing of a BLA submission for SRP-9003'. Case for later: the FDA may want LGMD2E patients dosed under sirolimus, or the sirolimus data may not change the risk-benefit (the FDA ties ELEVIDYS non-ambulatory dosing to the same data), and Sarepta restructured in 2025 to meet 2027 financial obligations. Not refused: SRP-9003 is the one LGMD programme the Restructuring did not suspend ('The Restructuring suspended all development of our LGMD programs with the exception of SRP-9003', 10-Q), Sarepta names it among its 2026 FDA discussions, and the FDA has said what it needs before accepting a BLA

column11: Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144, filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 'Key Patents & Regulatory Exclusivities': SRP-9003 composition-of-matter patents US 11,358,993 (expiring 2039) and EP 3 442 600 (2037), Owner/Licensor 'Nationwide'. Note 3 (Myonexus): acquired April 2019 for $178.3mm; 'The Company may also be required to make up to $200.0 million in additional payments to selling shareholders of Myonexus based on the achievement of certain sales-and regulatory-related milestones' across the five LGMD programmes, plus contingent payments 'upon the receipt and subsequent sale of a PRV with respect to a Myonexus product'. Myonexus's LGMD platform was licensed from Nationwide Children's Hospital (Myonexus release, businesswire.com/news/home/20190227005530/en/, via search summary). Genethon's 2019 collaboration covered micro-dystrophin only and was terminated in June 2024 (FY2024 10-K 0000950170-25-029973, Note 3)
column12: CEILING, and the caller's royalty test needs a decision. Sarepta owns SRP-9003 outright; no partner shares its economics. What is filed: milestones (up to $200mm to former Myonexus holders, sales and regulatory, shared across five programmes, none netted since the engine has no milestone line) and a PRV-sale contingency. What is not filed: any royalty on SRP-9003. Nationwide is the licensor of its key patents, and academic licences usually carry a running royalty, but no filing states one or gives a rate for this licence. The only Nationwide rate on file is the October 2018 micro-dystrophin licence for ELEVIDYS, 'lower single-digit royalties' (10-K Note 3), which does not cover SRP-9003. Held at 1.0 because no royalty is confirmed on the filed record; if the house treats Nationwide's licensorship as a royalty with no filed rate, this asset should be refused on that ground. Even with a rate, the netting (m - r) / m cannot be set: Sarepta has no cost rows in the book

column11: 0.86 per million: Fanin M et al., 'Genetic epidemiology of muscular dystrophies resulting from sarcoglycan gene mutations', J Med Genet 1997;34:973-7 (PMID 9429136, doi:10.1136/jmg.34.12.973), north-east Italy (2,319,147 inhabitants): primary sarcoglycanopathy prevalence 5.6 per million, with beta-sarcoglycan mutations in 2 of 13 patients, 5.6 x 2/13 = 0.86 per million. The same rate is the 'reported prevalence of 0.86 x 10^-6' for LGMDR4 in Iammarino MA et al. (Nationwide Children's, Mendell), J Neuromuscul Dis 2025 (PMID 40356354, doi:10.1177/22143602251339219, PMC13142873). Applied to 340,110,988 US residents at 1 July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024, the figure the zilovertamab, velzatinib and ianalumab seeds carry): 0.86e-6 x 340,110,988 = 292.5
column12: Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool 'Limb', 'Limb-Girdle' and 'LGMD' return nothing and epidemiology.csv has no LGMD row, so this is the first LGMD2E/R4 pool. The context's indication name covers all LGMDs; the pool is LGMD2E/R4 only, the label's disease. JUDGEMENT that an Italian 1997 rate from two patients transfers to the US. Case for higher: Iammarino reports a higher documented prevalence in 'some regions of the United States' from founder variants, and enrolled 30 carriers of the c.452C>G founder variant from one Plain community; Liu W et al., Genet Med 2019;21:2512-20 (PMID 31105274, gnomAD Bayesian estimate) found its LGMD2E estimate comparable with published epidemiology (search summary; its figure was not seen). Sarepta's 10-K puts all LGMDs at 1 in 14,500 to 1 in 123,000, and the 2025 sarcoglycanopathy review (J Neuromuscul Dis, doi:10.1177/22143602251324855) puts beta-sarcoglycanopathy at 15-30% of sarcoglycanopathies (Fanin's 2 of 13 is 15%). Case for lower: prevalence counts include undiagnosed or genetically unconfirmed patients who cannot be treated

column12: JUDGEMENT: the NTLA-2002 method (births times the population rate). A population rate understates birth prevalence where the disease shortens life (LGMDR4 cardiomyopathy), so this is a floor. The engine filters it by eligible_pct: 2.69 a year

column11: EMERGENE (NCT06246513) entry criteria: genetically confirmed LGMD2E/R4, ambulatory and non-ambulatory cohorts, aged 4 and over, AAVrh74 total binding antibody titers below 1:400 (trial listings via search summary; 10-Q: EMERGENE is SRP-9003-301). Seronegative share: 86.1% of genetically confirmed DMD patients aged 4 to 17 (107 eligible participants) had titers below 1:400 (Goedeker NL et al., Ther Adv Neurol Disord 2023;16:17562864221149781, PMID 36710722, doi:10.1177/17562864221149781)
column12: One filter, the AAVrh74 antibody exclusion: 292 x 0.861 = 251 eligible US patients plus 2.7 a year. Age is not filtered: LGMDR4 symptoms start at 5 to 16 years (Iammarino 2025), so few diagnosed patients are under 4 (the youngest of the 46 in the Nationwide cohort was 3.0 at enrollment). Ambulatory status is not filtered, because EMERGENE enrolled both. JUDGEMENT that DMD children's seroprevalence transfers; adults may carry more AAVrh74 antibodies. Case for lower: the FDA removed ELEVIDYS's non-ambulatory indication after fatal liver failure, the fatal SRP-9004 case was non-ambulatory, and the hold is tied to sirolimus data, so an SRP-9003 label could be ambulatory only: 63% of the Nationwide LGMDR4 cohort were ambulant (29 of 46, Iammarino Table 1; the abstract says 22, 55%), which would give 0.861 x 0.63 = 0.54

column11: Incumbent: ELEVIDYS, Sarepta's AAVrh74 gene therapy. US net revenue $200,356k (2023, launch June 2023), $820,791k (2024), $898,731k (2025) (Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144, filed 2026-03-02), Note 7). Revenue-parity patients at this seed's net price ($2.5152mm = 3.2 x (1 - 0.214)): 79.7, 326.3, 357.3. ELEVIDYS eligible pool: the book's DMD figures (11,952 prevalent, 367 a year; verified/DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251.json) x the same 0.861 seronegative share = 10,291 plus 316 a year, retention 0.9702 (the same stationary convention). Through the engine identity ELEVIDYS captured 0.75% of the eligible untreated pool in 2023, 3.10% in 2024 and 3.50% in 2025. The ramp below with peak 0.0351 reproduces 2024 (0.0309) and 2025 (0.0350)
column12: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on ELEVIDYS's 2025 capture, the first full year on its June 2024 broad label (ambulatory and non-ambulatory, aged 4 and over). The ELEVIDYS pool is not narrowed for age under 4 or exon 8-9 deletions, which understates its capture slightly. On SRP-9003's pool that is about 8 patients and $20mm a year from 2029, 33% of the eligible pool treated by 2039. Case for higher: the LGMD2E/R4 pool is small and concentrated, much of it known to Nationwide Children's (46 patients in one natural-history cohort, 30 in one founder community), so a site-driven launch could treat far more than 3.5% a year. Case for lower: ELEVIDYS's capture has fallen since the safety events, to $102.0mm in Q1 2026 and $98.1mm in Q2 2026 (8-Ks 0001193125-26-208966 and 0001193125-26-335056) on an ambulatory-only label, 159 patient-equivalents a year annualised, 1.6% of the all-DMD eligible pool (the ambulatory share of DMD is not sourced here, so the capture of its own label is not solved); SRP-9003 would launch under the same liver-safety overhang, likely with sirolimus
